name.zh-Hant: 烏魯魯–卡塔丘塔國家公園
name.zh-Hans: 乌卢鲁–卡塔丘塔国家公园

airspace.zh: 烏魯魯－卡塔丘塔國家公園是「無人機禁飛公園」：操作無人機須事先取得公園許可，且只有在特殊情況、並完成中央土地委員會的諮詢後才可能核准；為商業或公開目的拍攝烏魯魯或卡塔丘塔也須許可。實際飛行前請先確認澳洲民航安全局與公園的規定。
airspace.en: Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa is a no-drone park: operating a drone needs a park permit, approved only in exceptional circumstances after consultation with the Central Land Council; depicting Uluṟu or Kata Tjuṯa for commercial or public purposes also needs a permit. Check CASA and park rules before any real flight.

mutitjulu.note: Waterhole at the south side of the rock; approximate

centre.zh: 烏魯魯－卡塔丘塔文化中心

walpa.note: Gorge on the west side of the domes; approximate

plain.zh: 烏魯魯與卡塔丘塔之間的沙原
plain.en: Sand plain between Uluṟu and Kata Tjuṯa

resort.note: Visitor village outside the park; approximate

tagline.zh-Hant: 1873年的命名、1985年的歸還，到2019年停止攀登
tagline.en: A name in 1873, the handback of 1985, and the end of climbing in 2019

zh: 數萬年來，阿南古人生活在這片土地上。
烏魯魯與卡塔丘塔，是他們的家園與聖地。
en: For tens of thousands of years the Aṉangu have lived on this land.
Uluṟu and Kata Tjuṯa are their home and their sacred places.

zh: 1872年，探險家歐內斯特·賈爾斯看到卡塔丘塔。
他應植物學家米勒的請求，以符騰堡王后奧爾加命名為奧爾加山。
en: In 1872 the explorer Ernest Giles sighted Kata Tjuṯa.
At botanist von Mueller's request he named it Mount Olga, after Queen Olga of Württemberg.

zh: 1873年7月19日，測量員威廉·高斯看見烏魯魯。
他以南澳首席秘書亨利·艾爾斯之名，稱它為艾爾斯岩。
en: On 19 July 1873 the surveyor William Gosse sighted Uluṟu
and named it Ayers Rock, after South Australia's Chief Secretary, Sir Henry Ayers.

zh: 從此，這塊巨岩有了兩個名字。
一個來自阿南古人，一個來自殖民者。
en: From then on the rock had two names,
one from the Aṉangu and one from the colonists.

zh: 阿南古人和土地委員會長年爭取土地權。
1983年上任的霍克政府，終於宣布改變政策。
en: The Aṉangu and the land councils campaigned for years for their land.
The Hawke government, elected in 1983, finally announced a change.

zh: 1985年10月26日，總督史蒂芬在岩石下交出公園地契。
兩千多人見證了這一刻。
en: On 26 October 1985 Governor-General Sir Ninian Stephen handed over the title deeds
at the foot of the rock, before more than 2,000 people.

zh: 阿南古人隨即把公園租回給國家，租期99年。
公園由阿南古人佔多數的委員會共同管理。
en: The Aṉangu then leased the park back to the nation for 99 years,
to be jointly managed by a board with an Aṉangu majority.

zh: 1987年，公園因自然價值列入世界遺產。
1994年，又以文化景觀的身分再次登錄。
en: In 1987 the park joined the World Heritage List for its natural values,
and in 1994 it was listed again as a cultural landscape.

zh: 它是世界上第二座以文化景觀列入世界遺產的國家公園。
登錄的理由，是人與土地之間的關係。
en: It was the second national park in the world to be listed as a cultural landscape,
recognising the bond between people and land.

zh: 1993年起，官方採用雙重名稱。
2002年，順序改成「烏魯魯／艾爾斯岩」。
en: A dual-naming policy began in 1993,
and in 2002 the order became Uluṟu / Ayers Rock.

zh: 2017年11月1日，公園委員會決定禁止攀登。
2019年10月26日起，正式停止攀登烏魯魯。
en: On 1 November 2017 the park board voted to ban climbing,
and from 26 October 2019 the climb was closed.

zh: 理由包括岩石對阿南古人的精神意義，
攀登路線穿過一條神聖的路徑，以及遊客的安全。
en: Reasons included the rock's spiritual importance to the Aṉangu,
a climbing route crossing a sacred track, and visitor safety.

zh: 從被命名、被歸還，到不再被攀登，
這塊土地的歷史，回到了它原本的主人手中。
en: From naming to handback to the end of the climb,
the story of this land has returned to its first custodians.

title.en: Tjukurpa: the Law of the Land

tagline.zh-Hant: 阿南古人的知識、岩畫與水潭，以及給旅人的請求
tagline.en: Aṉangu knowledge, rock art and waterholes, and a request to visitors

zh: 對阿南古人來說，烏魯魯不只是一塊岩石。
它承載著「楚庫帕」，一套連結人與土地的信仰與律法。
en: To the Aṉangu, Uluṟu is not just a rock.
It holds Tjukurpa, a religious philosophy linking people to their land.

zh: 楚庫帕說明了世界如何形成，也規範人該如何生活。
公園的管理，以楚庫帕為核心。
en: Tjukurpa explains how the world came to be and how people should live.
It is at the centre of how the park is managed.

zh: 岩石南側的穆蒂圖魯水潭，是沙漠中珍貴的水源。
岩石周圍有泉水、水潭、岩洞與古老的岩畫。
en: Mutitjulu Waterhole on the south side is a precious source of water.
Around the rock are springs, waterholes, caves and ancient paintings.

zh: 岩畫與岩刻，記錄著代代相傳的故事。
這些故事，透過歌、舞與畫流傳下來。
en: Paintings and carvings record stories passed down the generations,
carried on in song, dance and art.

zh: 文化中心由阿南古人參與規劃，介紹他們的文化。
公園的解說，以阿南古人的知識為主。
en: The Cultural Centre, shaped with the Aṉangu, introduces their culture.
Their knowledge is the main voice in explaining the park.

zh: 岩石底部有些地方是神聖的場所。
阿南古人請遊客不要拍攝這些地點，現場會有標示。
en: Some places at the base of the rock are sacred.
The Aṉangu ask visitors not to photograph them; signs mark where.

zh: 黃昏時，遊客聚在觀景區，看岩石轉紅。
紅色的岩石，是澳洲最熟悉的風景之一。
en: At dusk visitors gather at the viewing area to watch the rock turn red,
one of Australia's most familiar sights.

zh: 2000年時，每年的遊客已超過四十萬人。
大多數人住在公園外的尤拉拉度假村。
en: By 2000 more than 400,000 people were visiting each year,
most of them staying at Yulara outside the park.

zh: 尤拉拉位在公園北方。
從這裡，可以同時望見烏魯魯和卡塔丘塔。
en: Yulara lies north of the park.
From here both Uluṟu and Kata Tjuṯa can be seen.

zh: 卡塔丘塔的名字，意思是「許多頭」。
這裡也是阿南古人的聖地。
en: Kata Tjuṯa means "many heads".
It too is a sacred place for the Aṉangu.

zh: 風之谷步道，讓遊客走進圓頂之間。
炎熱的日子，部分步道會封閉。
en: The Valley of the Winds walk leads in among the domes;
parts of it close on very hot days.

zh: 攀登停止後，遊客改為繞著岩石底部步行。
近距離看見水潭與岩洞，也聽見阿南古人的故事。
en: Since the climb closed, visitors walk around the base instead,
seeing the waterholes and caves up close and hearing Aṉangu stories.

zh: 尊重這片土地的方式，就是聽它的主人怎麼說。
在烏魯魯，旅人也成了楚庫帕故事的一部分。
en: To respect this land is to listen to its custodians.
At Uluṟu, visitors become part of the story of Tjukurpa.

tagline.zh-Hant: 雨水從巨岩流下、沙原與沙丘，以及沙漠動植物
tagline.en: Rain running off the rock, sand plains and dunes, and desert life

zh: 烏魯魯一帶是乾燥的沙漠，雨水稀少。
紅色的沙原上，長著耐旱的草與灌木。
en: The country around Uluṟu is dry desert with little rain.
Hardy grasses and shrubs grow on the red sand plain.

zh: 下雨時，雨水沿著岩面迅速流下。
巨岩把雨水集中到底部的水潭。
en: When it rains, water pours quickly down the rock face.
The rock gathers it into the waterholes at its foot.

zh: 大雨時，岩面上會出現一道道短暫的瀑布。
雨停之後，瀑布很快就消失。
en: In heavy rain, short-lived waterfalls stream down the rock.
Soon after the rain stops, they are gone.

zh: 穆蒂圖魯水潭，在乾季也常常有水。
水潭周圍，聚集著鳥類與其他動物。
en: Mutitjulu Waterhole often holds water even in the dry season,
drawing birds and other animals around it.

zh: 岩石底部的陰影與水分，讓植物長得比平原茂盛。
巨岩，在沙漠中創造了一個小小的綠洲。
en: Shade and moisture at the base let plants grow thicker than on the plain.
The rock makes a small oasis in the desert.

zh: 沙原上長著一叢叢的鬣刺草。
它尖銳的葉子，能減少水分散失。
en: Clumps of spinifex grass dot the sand plain,
their spiky leaves cutting water loss.

zh: 沙丘之間，長著高大的沙漠橡木。
它們的根，能深入地下尋找水。
en: Tall desert oaks grow between the dunes,
their roots reaching deep for water.

zh: 卡塔丘塔的谷地比較陰涼。
雨後，谷裡的溪流和水潭會短暫出現。
en: Kata Tjuṯa's valleys are cooler and more sheltered.
After rain, creeks and pools appear there for a while.

zh: 圓頂之間的谷地，是動物躲避酷熱的地方。
許多動物在清晨和黃昏才出來活動。
en: The valleys between the domes are refuges from the heat.
Many animals come out only at dawn and dusk.

zh: 沙漠中住著許多爬蟲類，例如身上長滿尖刺的棘蜥。
牠們適應了白天炎熱、夜晚寒冷的環境。
en: Many reptiles live in this desert, such as the spiny thorny devil,
adapted to scorching days and cold nights.

zh: 澳洲野犬、袋鼠與各種鳥類，也在沙原上活動。
牠們多半在比較涼爽的時段覓食。
en: Dingoes, kangaroos and many birds also range across the plain,
mostly feeding in the cooler hours.

zh: 阿南古人用火來照顧土地。
小規模的燒除，能讓植物更新，也減少大火的風險。
en: The Aṉangu use fire to care for the country.
Small burns renew the plants and lower the risk of big fires.

zh: 公園的管理，結合了傳統知識與現代科學。
這片看似空曠的沙漠，其實充滿生命。
en: Park management combines traditional knowledge with modern science.
This seemingly empty desert is full of life.

zh: 遠離城市的沙漠，夜空幾乎沒有光害。
天黑之後，銀河清楚地橫過天空。
en: Far from any city, the desert night is almost free of light pollution.
After dark the Milky Way arches clearly overhead.

zh: 雨水從巨岩流下，養活了水潭邊的生命；
在紅色的中心，每一滴水都很珍貴。
en: Rain running off the rock feeds the life around its waterholes;
in the Red Centre, every drop counts.

title.en: Two Great Rocks in the Desert

tagline.zh-Hant: 五億多年前的沉積、翻轉的岩層，與36座圓頂
tagline.en: Sediments over 500 million years old, upended layers, and 36 domes

zh: 澳洲中部的沙漠裡，突起一塊巨岩：烏魯魯。
它比周圍平原高出348公尺，海拔863公尺。
en: In the desert of central Australia rises a great rock: Uluṟu.
It stands 348 metres above the plain, 863 metres above sea level.

zh: 它的周長約9.4公里。
位置在愛麗斯泉西南方約335公里。
en: It is about 9.4 kilometres around,
some 335 kilometres south-west of Alice Springs.

zh: 烏魯魯主要由長石砂岩構成。
這種砂岩含有大量長石，形成於約五億五千萬到五億三千萬年前。
en: Uluṟu is mostly arkose, a sandstone rich in feldspar,
laid down some 550 to 530 million years ago.

zh: 岩層原本是水平沉積的。
後來地殼運動，把它們翻轉到幾乎垂直。
en: The layers were first laid down flat.
Later movements of the crust tipped them almost on end.

zh: 仔細看岩壁上一條條平行的紋路，
那就是被翻轉過來的岩層。
en: Look closely at the parallel ribs on the rock face:
they are those upended layers.

zh: 我們看到的，只是岩體的一小部分。
大部分岩層，延伸到平原底下。
en: What we see is only a small part of the formation.
Most of it continues beneath the plain.

zh: 岩石裡的氧化鐵，讓它呈現紅色。
清晨與黃昏，岩石的顏色會跟著陽光改變。
en: Iron oxide gives the rock its red colour.
At dawn and dusk its hue changes with the light.

zh: 往西25公里，是另一群巨岩：卡塔丘塔。
中間是一片平坦的沙原。
en: Twenty-five kilometres to the west lies another group of rocks: Kata Tjuṯa.
Between them stretches a flat sand plain.

zh: 卡塔丘塔由36座圓頂組成，分布在約21.7平方公里內。
它的岩石是礫岩：卵石與巨石被砂岩膠結在一起。
en: Kata Tjuṯa is 36 domes spread over about 21.7 square kilometres.
Its rock is conglomerate: cobbles and boulders cemented by sandstone.

zh: 最高的奧爾加山，比平原高出546公尺。
它比烏魯魯還高198公尺。
en: The highest dome, Mount Olga, rises 546 metres above the plain,
198 metres higher than Uluṟu.

zh: 圓頂之間，是深深的谷地。
風之谷步道，就從圓頂之間穿過。
en: Deep valleys run between the domes.
The Valley of the Winds walk threads its way through them.

zh: 卡塔丘塔的岩層只微微傾斜，
和幾乎垂直的烏魯魯很不一樣。
en: Kata Tjuṯa's layers are only gently tilted,
quite unlike the near-vertical beds of Uluṟu.

zh: 從正上方看，36座圓頂像一群擠在一起的頭。
卡塔丘塔的意思，正是「許多頭」。
en: From straight above, the 36 domes look like heads crowded together.
Kata Tjuṯa means "many heads".

zh: 兩群巨岩周圍，是幾乎平坦的沙原。
較軟的岩石早已被侵蝕，只剩下最堅硬的部分。
en: Around both groups the sand plain is almost flat.
Softer rock wore away long ago, leaving only the hardest parts.

zh: 五億年的沉積、翻轉、抬升與侵蝕，
留下了沙漠中這兩座巨岩。
en: Five hundred million years of deposition, folding, uplift and erosion
have left these two great rocks in the desert.
